criteria.criterion: Both shard-test-executing subprocesses in `execute_shard()` — the baseline `pytest` and the `mutmut run` mutant test-run — are wrapped in an OS-enforced sandbox denying writes outside an explicit allow-list. The venv is deliberately EXCLUDED from it.
The enforcement test trips the deny under `mutmut run` specifically, not only under the baseline `pytest`.

The sandbox demonstrably DENIES: a probe writing outside the allow-list exits non-zero and the file is absent afterward, while the same probe inside succeeds. Asserting wrapper argv alone does not satisfy this.

macOS uses Seatbelt `sandbox-exec` with a generated `(allow default)` + `(deny file-write*)` + allow-list profile, reproducing the three probes. `sandbox-exec` is Apple-deprecated, so `_seatbelt_works` requires an observed DENIAL plus a liveness marker.
Linux uses `bwrap`, probed at runtime, and fails closed without it. No `unshare` fallback.

citation.description: Ticket comment: 'Linux enforcement was measured by hand in a ubuntu:24.04 container (write outside DENIED, write inside succeeded, rm -rf <protected>/* DENIED with target surviving), and the missing gating lane is tracked as 0d22-f664-77e1-495f.'

criteria.criterion: The Linux write-deny is proven ON Linux, not inferred from macOS: the three probes were measured by hand in a ubuntu:24.04 container.
The sandbox wrapper preserves the existing `mutmut run --max-children 1` concurrency contract asserted at `tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py:948`.

On a WORKSTATION with no sandbox mechanism the run ABORTS non-zero with a message naming `REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED`; the CI-runner exception is the criterion below, and the two are exhaustive.
`REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED=1` waives the sandbox and logs at WARNING; a silent fallback is rejected.
Enforcement is an OS facility invoked in-process, never a CI-provider feature, and works from a laptop with no CI involved.

`HOME` is set to a non-existent path for both sandboxed subprocesses so adjacent home-directory writes fail loudly. Verified by RUNNING a child and asserting the HOME it observes, plus a binding test tying both wrapped `_run` calls to the hardened env — each proven RED.

`probe()` verifies BOTH mechanisms FUNCTIONALLY, never by `shutil.which`. Verified by `test_bwrap_present_but_unable_to_namespace_is_not_offered` and `test_seatbelt_present_but_not_enforcing_is_not_offered`, each proven RED.

On a CI runner (`CI` truthy) with no mechanism the gate proceeds UNSANDBOXED with a WARNING; on a workstation it still ABORTS. Verified by `test_ci_runner_proceeds_unsandboxed_with_a_warning` and `test_workstation_still_aborts_when_no_sandbox`.
Bubblewrap is installed on the Linux CI lanes (`_build-and-test.yml`, `_mutation.yml`) so `bwrap` EXISTS there; macOS needs none.
A usable sandbox is used even on CI — `CI` is a fallback for the ABSENCE of a mechanism, never a licence to skip a working one. Verified by `test_a_working_sandbox_is_used_even_on_ci`.
